title: fgetl
summary: Read the next line without newline characters in MATLAB and RunMat.

gpu_support.notes: Runs entirely on the host CPU. Provider-resident file identifiers are a gated RunMat extension and are gathered before host I/O.

description: `fgetl(fid)` reads the next line from a text file and removes trailing line terminators from the returned character row vector. End-of-file signaling and file-position behavior follow MATLAB semantics, so empty lines remain distinguishable from EOF.
behaviors: `tline = fgetl(fid)` reads from the current file position to the next line terminator or to end-of-file when no terminator is found.

Line terminators are consumed but not included in the returned character row vector. RunMat recognises `
`, `
`, `
`, and ``; the `
` pair is consumed as one newline sequence.
When the file is empty or the file position indicator is already at end-of-file, `fgetl` returns the numeric sentinel `-1`.
An empty line returns an empty character row vector, not `-1`.
Lines are decoded using the text encoding recorded by `fopen`.

examples.description: Read the first line of a file without the newline
Read a file line by line
Distinguish an empty line from end of file
Read a final line without a trailing newline

faqs.question: What does `fgetl` return at end-of-file?
faqs.answer: When no characters can be read because the file position indicator is at end-of-file, `fgetl` returns the numeric value `-1`.

faqs.question: How does `fgetl` differ from `fgets`?
faqs.answer: `fgetl` removes newline characters from the returned line, while `fgets` keeps them. Use `fgetl` for newline-free line processing and `fgets` when terminator bytes matter.

faqs.question: What happens for a blank line?
faqs.answer: A blank line returns an empty character row vector. Only EOF before any characters are read returns `-1`.

faqs.question: Can I call `fgetl` on files opened for writing only?
faqs.answer: No. The file must be opened with read permission (for example `'r'`, `'r+'`, or `'w+'`). Calling `fgetl` on a write-only identifier raises an error.

points: `fileID` is an integer-valued double file handle returned by `fopen`. Typed-integer, single-precision, and provider-resident identifiers are independently gated RunMat extensions. The file must be opened with read permission (`'r'`, `'r+'`, `'w+'`, or `'a+'`).
`line` is a character row vector without the trailing line terminator. When the file position is already at end-of-file, `fgetl` returns the numeric sentinel `-1`.

gpu_behavior: `fgetl` is a host-only operation. Provider-resident identifiers are a gated RunMat extension; when enabled, RunMat gathers the scalar before reading and returns a regular host value.
